results.title: Ball in the word metric
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite subset $S$ of a group $\Gamma$ and a natural number $n$, the ball $B_S(n)$ of radius $n$ is the set of products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$, the empty product $1$ included.

results.title: Polynomial growth with respect to a finite subset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a finite subset of a group $\Gamma$, and let $B_S(n)$ be the ball of radius $n$ for $S$, the set of products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. Then $\Gamma$ has polynomial growth with respect to $S$ if there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that for every natural number $n$ the ball $B_S(n)$ has at most $C\,(n + 1)^d$ elements.

results.title: Boundary of a finite subset of a group

results.title: Residually nilpotent group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is residually nilpotent if for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is nilpotent.

results.title: Residually torsion-free nilpotent group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is residually torsion-free nilpotent if for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is nilpotent and torsion-free, that is, every nontrivial element of $G/N$ has infinite order.

results.title: Mikhailov–Passi question on free central extensions (Kourovka 16.65)

results.title: Free central extensions need not be residually nilpotent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a free group $F$ and a normal subgroup $R$ of $F$ such that $F/R$ is finitely presented and residually torsion-free nilpotent, while $F/[F, R]$ is not residually nilpotent; here $[F, R]$ is the subgroup of $F$ generated by all commutators $[f, r]$ with $f \in F$ and $r \in R$.

results.title: Labos prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $\pi(x)$ for the number of primes $p \le x$. For natural numbers $n$ and $L$, $L$ is the $n$-th Labos prime when $n \ge 1$, $L \ge 1$, $\pi(L) - \pi(\lfloor L/2 \rfloor) = n$, and no integer $m$ with $1 \le m < L$ satisfies $\pi(m) - \pi(\lfloor m/2 \rfloor) = n$; that is, $L$ is the least positive integer with $\pi(L) - \pi(\lfloor L/2 \rfloor) = n$.

results.title: Primes satisfying the Ramanujan counting condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function. For natural numbers $R$ and $n$, $R$ satisfies the Ramanujan counting condition for $n$ when $R$ is prime and $\pi(R) - \pi(R/2) = n$.

results.title: The $n$-th Ramanujan prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function. For natural numbers $R$ and $n$, $R$ is the $n$-th Ramanujan prime when $n \ge 1$, $R$ is a prime with $\pi(R) - \pi(R/2) = n$, and every prime $p$ with $\pi(p) - \pi(p/2) = n$ satisfies $p \le R$. That is, $R$ is the largest prime satisfying the Ramanujan counting condition for $n$.

results.title: Counting members of a set up to a real bound

results.title: Laishram's upper bound for Ramanujan primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_k$ denote the $k$-th prime, so that $p_1 = 2$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $R$, if $R$ is the $n$-th Ramanujan prime (which entails $n \ge 1$), then $R < p_{3n}$.

results.title: Bertrand's postulate in block form
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ there are $i < n$ and a prime $p > n$ such that $p$ divides $n + 1 + i$. Thus one of the $n$ consecutive integers $n + 1, \dots, 2n$ has a prime divisor greater than $n$.

results.title: Prime divisors above $n$ of a block term divide the binomial coefficient
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j < n$, and let $r$ be a prime with $r > n$. If $r$ divides $k + j$, then $r$ divides $\binom{k+n-1}{n}$.

results.title: A block term divisible by the block length plus two

results.title: Fixed point property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $K$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ has the fixed point property when every continuous map $f \colon K \to K$ has a fixed point, that is, a point $x \in K$ with $f(x) = x$.

results.title: Nonseparating planar continuum conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjecture asserts that every nonempty, compact, path-connected subset $K$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ is connected (that is, $K$ does not separate the plane) has the fixed point property: every continuous map $f \colon K \to K$ has a point $x \in K$ with $f(x) = x$.

results.title: Path-connected nonseparating plane continua have the fixed point property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty, compact, path-connected subset of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ is connected. Then $K$ has the fixed point property: every continuous map $f \colon K \to K$ has a point $x \in K$ with $f(x) = x$.

results.title: Kripke semantic values
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a context $\Gamma$, the semantic values of a simple type in $\Gamma$ are defined by recursion on the type. At a base type $b$ they are the neutral terms of type $b$ in $\Gamma$ (variables applied to zero or more normal arguments). At an arrow type $A \Rightarrow B$ a semantic value is a family that, for every context $\Delta$ and every renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, maps semantic values of type $A$ in…

results.title: Renaming a semantic value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, a simple type $A$ and a semantic value $v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the renamed value is the semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$ defined by cases on $A$. At a base type it is the neutral term $v$ with its free variables renamed by $\rho$. At an arrow type $A = B \Rightarrow C$ it sends a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to a context $\Theta$…

results.title: Semantic environments for normalization by evaluation
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For contexts $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$, a semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$ assigns to every variable of $\Gamma$, of any type $A$, a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$.

results.title: Renaming a semantic environment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Delta$ to a context $\Theta$ and a semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$, the renamed environment is the semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Theta$ that sends each variable $x$ of type $A$ to the semantic value $\eta(x)$ renamed along $\rho$ at type $A$.

results.title: Extending a semantic environment by one variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a semantic value $a$ of type $A$ in a context $\Delta$ and a semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$, the extended environment is the semantic environment for the context $A :: \Gamma$ (the context $\Gamma$ with a new innermost variable of type $A$) in $\Delta$ that sends the new innermost variable to $a$ and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(x)$.

results.title: The identity semantic environment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a context $\Gamma$, the identity environment is the semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Gamma$ that sends each variable $x$ of type $A$ to the reflection at type $A$ of the neutral term $x$. Reflection turns a neutral term into a semantic value of the same type in the same context.

results.title: Evaluation into the Kripke semantic domain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $T$ in context $\Gamma$ and let $\eta$ be a semantic environment interpreting every variable of $\Gamma$ as a semantic value in context $\Delta$. The evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(t, \eta)$ is the semantic value of type $T$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: a variable $x$ evaluates to $\eta(x)$; an application $f\,a$ evaluates to the semantic function…

results.title: Normalization by evaluation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normal form is the beta-normal, eta-long term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ obtained by reifying, at type $A$, the evaluation of $t$ in the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$, which interprets each variable as the reflection of that variable.

results.title: Normalization of terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normalized term is the term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ underlying the beta-normal, eta-long normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.

results.title: Reflection commutes with renaming
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type $A$, every renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, and every neutral term $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, transporting the semantic value obtained by reflecting $n$ at type $A$ along $\rho$ gives the reflection at type $A$ of the neutral term $n$ renamed by $\rho$.

results.title: The identity environment under a binder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context, $A$ a type, and $\Gamma, A$ the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Transport the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$ (which reflects each variable as a neutral value) along the weakening renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma, A$ that sends each variable to its successor, and extend the result by the reflection at type $A$ of the newest variable of $\Gamma, A$.…

results.title: Evaluation respects pointwise equal environments
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and let $\xi$ and $\zeta$ be semantic environments interpreting the variables of $\Gamma$ in a context $\Delta$. If $\xi(x) = \zeta(x)$ for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, of any type, then evaluating $t$ in $\xi$ and evaluating $t$ in $\zeta$ give the same semantic value.

results.title: Evaluating a neutral term reflects it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every neutral term $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, evaluating the underlying term of $n$ in the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$ gives the reflection of $n$ at type $A$.

results.title: Normal forms are fixed points of normalization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every beta-normal, eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ by evaluation returns the normal form $n$ itself.

results.title: Renormalizing a computed normal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of the normal form that normalization by evaluation computes from $t$ gives the same term as normalizing $t$.

results.title: Normalization by evaluation is idempotent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the normalized term of $t$ by evaluation gives the normalized term of $t$ again.

results.title: Normalization fixes the terms of normal forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ returns that term unchanged.

results.title: Erasing normal forms is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, two eta-long normal forms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ with the same underlying term are equal.

results.title: Canonical terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical when it is the underlying term of some beta-normal, eta-long normal form of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$.

results.title: Canonical terms are the fixed points of normalization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical if and only if normalization by evaluation maps $t$ to itself, that is, the term underlying the normal form computed for $t$ is $t$.

results.title: Normalized terms are canonical
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the term obtained by normalizing $t$ by evaluation is canonical.

results.title: Renaming preserves canonical terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical, then for every renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the term obtained by renaming $t$ along $\rho$ is canonical.

results.title: Certified canonical terms
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ and a type $A$, a certified canonical term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ together with a proof that $t$ is a fixed point of normalization by evaluation: the term underlying the normal form computed for $t$ is $t$ itself.

results.title: Normal forms as canonical terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The canonical term of an eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the underlying term of $n$, certified to be a fixed point of normalization.

results.title: The normal form of a canonical term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a canonical term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, that is, a term that normalization returns unchanged, its normal form is the eta-long normal form that normalization by evaluation computes from $t$.

results.title: Canonical terms have a unique normal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. If $t$ is canonical, then there is exactly one beta-normal, eta-long normal form of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ whose underlying term is $t$.

results.title: Kripke realization relation for NbE
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. For a context $\Gamma$, an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, a type $A$, a Kripke semantic value $v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and an element $d$ of the denotation of $A$ under $I$, the relation "$v$ realizes $d$ at $\eta$" is defined by recursion on $A$. At a base type, $v$ is a neutral term, and $v$ realizes $d$ when the denotation of $v$, read as a term, in $\eta$…

results.title: Realization is stable under renaming
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $v$ be a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ that realizes an element $d$ of the denotation of $A$ at an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$. If $\rho : \Gamma \to \Delta$ is a renaming and $\theta$ is an environment for $\Delta$ with $\theta \circ \rho = \eta$, then the transport of $v$ along $\rho$ realizes $d$ at $\theta$.

results.title: Realization of environments
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types, contexts $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$, an environment $\theta$ for $\Delta$ in $I$, a Kripke semantic environment $\xi$ assigning to each variable of $\Gamma$ a semantic value in $\Delta$, and an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$. Then $\xi$ realizes $\eta$ at $\theta$ when for every type $A$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the semantic value $\xi(x)$…

results.title: Fundamental lemma for NbE evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, let $\xi$ be a Kripke semantic environment assigning to each variable of $\Gamma$ a semantic value in context $\Delta$, and let $\eta$ and $\theta$ be environments in $I$ for $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$. If $\xi$ realizes $\eta$ at $\theta$, then the NbE evaluation of $t$ in $\xi$ realizes the denotation of $t$ in $\eta$ at…

results.title: The identity semantic environment realizes every environment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types and an environment $\eta$ for a context $\Gamma$ in $I$. Then the identity Kripke semantic environment on $\Gamma$, which reflects each variable as a neutral value, realizes $\eta$ at $\eta$.

results.title: NbE preserves denotation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, the NbE normal form of $t$ has the same denotation in $\eta$ as $t$.

results.title: Every term is semantically equal to its NbE normal form in each model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, $t$ and its NbE normal form are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment for $\Gamma$ in $I$.

results.title: Every term is model-equal to its NbE normal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is model-equal to its NbE normal form.

results.title: Equal NbE normal forms imply model equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ have the same NbE normal form, then $t$ and $u$ are model-equal.

results.title: Coordinator states
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: In two-phase commit the coordinator is in one of three states: waiting (collecting votes), committed (it has decided commit) or aborted (it has decided abort).

results.title: Participant states in two-phase commit
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A participant is in one of four states: working (it has not voted), prepared (it voted yes and waits for the decision), committed, or aborted (it voted no, or learned of an abort).

results.title: Global states of two-phase commit
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a set $P$ of participants, a global state consists of a coordinator state together with a participant state for each participant $p \in P$.

results.title: Two-phase commit actions
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The actions of the two-phase commit protocol over a set $P$ of participants are: a participant $p \in P$ votes yes; a participant $p$ votes no; the coordinator decides commit; the coordinator decides abort; a participant $p$ learns the commit decision; and a participant $p$ learns the abort decision.

results.title: Updating one participant's state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a global state $s$, a participant $p$ and a participant state $x$, the updated state has the same coordinator state as $s$, gives participant $p$ the state $x$, and leaves the state of every other participant unchanged.

results.title: Transitions of two-phase commit
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The protocol steps from a global state $s$ to a global state $t$ by an action exactly in the following cases. A working participant $p$ may vote yes, after which $p$ is prepared, or vote no, after which $p$ is aborted. If the coordinator is waiting and every participant is prepared, the coordinator may decide commit, after which it is committed. If the coordinator is waiting, it may decide abort, after which it is…

results.title: Two-phase commit as a transition system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $P$ of participants, the labelled transition system whose states are the global states of the protocol, whose labels are the protocol actions, and whose transitions are the protocol steps.

results.title: Initial state of two-phase commit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial state of the two-phase commit protocol: the coordinator is waiting and every participant is working.

results.title: Reachable states of two-phase commit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A global state $s$ is reachable when some finite sequence of protocol actions leads by protocol steps from the initial state, in which the coordinator is waiting and every participant is working, to $s$.

results.title: Reachable states are closed under steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a global state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol is reachable and some action takes $s$ to $t$ in one protocol step, then $t$ is reachable.

results.title: Two-phase commit invariant
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A global state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol satisfies the invariant when two conditions hold: if the coordinator has committed, then every participant is prepared or committed; and every committed participant has a committed coordinator.

results.title: Multistep transitions preserve the two-phase commit invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a state $s$ of the two-phase commit protocol satisfies the inductive invariant and a state $t$ is reached from $s$ by a finite sequence of transitions, then $t$ satisfies the invariant.

results.title: The two-phase commit invariant holds in reachable states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $P$ of participants, every global state of the two-phase commit protocol that is reachable from the initial state satisfies the inductive invariant, that is, both of the following hold: if the coordinator has committed, then every participant is prepared or committed; and every committed participant has a committed coordinator.

results.title: Atomicity between participants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $P$ of participants, in every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant $p$ has committed, then no participant $q$ has aborted.

results.title: Validity for the coordinator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided commit, then every participant voted yes, that is, every participant is prepared or committed.

results.title: Validity for participants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has committed, then every participant voted yes, that is, every participant is prepared or committed.

results.title: An aborted participant rules out a coordinator commit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has aborted, then the coordinator has not decided commit.

results.title: A committed participant has a committed coordinator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if some participant has committed, then the coordinator has committed.

results.title: A committed coordinator has no aborted participant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided commit, then no participant has aborted.

results.title: An aborted coordinator has no committed participant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In every reachable state of the two-phase commit protocol, if the coordinator has decided abort, then no participant has committed.

results.title: Stochastic mass-action propensity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stochastic mass-action propensity of reaction `r` in state `x` (molecule counts): `k r * ∏_s x_s (x_s - 1) ⋯ (x_s - src_s + 1)`, the falling factorial `Nat.descFactorial x_s src_s` (it vanishes when `x_s < src_s`). Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz (2010), §2.

results.title: State after one reaction firing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The state reached from `x` by one firing of reaction `r`, `x - src r + prod r` (meaningful when `src r ≤ x`, the only case in which the propensity is nonzero).

results.title: State before one reaction firing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The state from which one firing of reaction `r` leads to `x`, `x - prod r + src r` (meaningful when `prod r ≤ x`).

results.title: Product-form Poisson weight of a state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The product-form Poisson weight `∏_s c_s ^ x_s e^{-c_s} / Nat.factorial x_s` of a state `x`.

results.title: Generator of the mass-action chain on a finite state class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generator of the stochastic mass-action chain restricted to a finite set `Ω` of states: `Q x y = ∑_r λ_r(x) ([fire r x = y] - [x = y])`. It is a rate matrix when `Ω` is closed under firing (`isRateMatrix_classGenerator`).

results.title: Global balance of the product-form Poisson weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Global balance of the product-form Poisson weights (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1): if `c` is complex balanced for the deterministic mass-action system with rate constants `k`, then at every state `x` the total outflow `π(x) ∑_r λ_r(x)` equals the total inflow `∑_{r : prod r ≤ x} π(x - prod r + src r) λ_r(x - prod r + src r)` for `π = poissonWeight c`. This is an algebraic identity valid for all real `k`…

results.title: Restricted mass-action generator is a rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The restricted generator is a rate matrix when the rate constants are nonnegative and `Ω` is closed under the reactions.

results.title: Anderson–Craciun–Kurtz on a finite class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Anderson–Craciun–Kurtz on a finite class (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1–4.2): if `c` is complex balanced and every state of `Ω` from which a reaction leads into `Ω` lies in `Ω` (`hbwd`), the Poisson weights restricted to `Ω` are invariant for the restricted generator: `π Q = 0`, for all real `k` and `c`. For a closed communicating class of a weakly reversible network with positive rate constants `hbwd`…

results.title: Normalized Poisson stationary law on a finite state class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Poisson weights normalized on a finite set `Ω` of states.

results.title: Stationary law of the stochastic mass-action chain on a finite class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Stationary law of the stochastic mass-action chain on a finite class (Anderson, Craciun & Kurtz 2010, Thm 4.1–4.2). Let the rate constants be nonnegative, `c > 0` complex balanced, and `Ω` a nonempty finite set of states closed under the reactions in both directions. Then the restricted generator is a rate matrix, and the normalized product-form Poisson law `π(x) ∝ ∏_s c_s^{x_s} e^{-c_s} / Nat.factorial x_s` on `Ω`…

results.title: Reaction fluxes proportional to enzyme levels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Reaction rates `v_i(e, s) = e_i f_i(s)` proportional to enzyme levels `e`.

results.title: Steady-state fluxes along a steady-state map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The steady-state fluxes `J(e) = v(e, σ(e))` along a steady-state map `σ`.

results.title: Flux control coefficient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The flux control coefficient `C^{J_j}_{e_i} = (e_i / J_j) ∂J_j/∂e_i`. It is meaningful when `J_j ≠ 0` and the steady-state flux is differentiable at `e`; otherwise Lean's `x / 0 = 0` and `fderiv` of a non-differentiable map, `0`, give junk values.

results.title: Concentration control coefficient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The concentration control coefficient `C^{s_m}_{e_i} = (e_i / s_m) ∂s_m/∂e_i`, meaningful for a positive concentration `s_m` and a steady state differentiable at `e`.

results.title: Elasticity of a reaction rate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The elasticity `ε^{v_i}_{s_m} = (s_m / v_i) ∂v_i/∂s_m`, meaningful for a nonzero rate `v_i` and a rate law differentiable at `s`.

results.title: Regular steady state of a metabolic network
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A regular steady state at enzyme levels `e₀`: `σ` is differentiable at `e₀`, the rate laws are differentiable at `σ e₀`, `N v(e, σ e) = 0` for `e` near `e₀`, and the Jacobian `δ ↦ N ∂_s v(e₀, σ e₀) δ` is injective (it is square, so this is its invertibility).

results.title: Regular steady states exist by the implicit function theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `s₀` is a steady state at enzyme levels `e₀`, the rate laws are continuously differentiable at `s₀`, and the Jacobian `δ ↦ N (e₀ ⊙ f'(s₀) δ)` is injective, then the steady state continues to a map `σ` with `σ e₀ = s₀` satisfying `IsRegularSteadyState`.

results.title: Concentration summation theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Concentration summation theorem (Heinrich & Rapoport 1974): for a positive steady-state concentration `s_m`, `∑_i C^{s_m}_{e_i} = 0`. The positivity hypothesis is the domain on which the scaled concentration control coefficients have their biological meaning.

results.title: Flux summation theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Flux summation theorem (Kacser & Burns 1973; Heinrich & Rapoport 1974): for a nonzero steady-state flux `J_j`, `∑_i C^{J_j}_{e_i} = 1`.

results.title: Flux connectivity theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Flux connectivity theorem (Kacser & Burns 1973): when all steady-state fluxes are nonzero, `∑_i C^{J_j}_{e_i} ε^{v_i}_{s_m} = 0` for every flux `J_j` and metabolite `s_m`.

results.title: Feasible fluxes of flux balance analysis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The feasible fluxes of flux balance analysis: `S v = b`, `l ≤ v ≤ u`.

results.title: Optimal value of flux balance analysis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The optimal value `max {c ⬝ᵥ v | S v = b, l ≤ v ≤ u}` of flux balance analysis (the supremum; it is `0` by convention when the problem is infeasible).

results.title: Dual feasibility for flux balance analysis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Dual feasibility for flux balance analysis: `y` prices the metabolites, `α, β ≥ 0` the upper and lower flux bounds, and `Sᵀ y + α - β = c`.

results.title: Dual objective of flux balance analysis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dual objective `b ⬝ᵥ y + u ⬝ᵥ α - l ⬝ᵥ β`.

results.title: Feasible flux balance problem attains its optimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A feasible flux balance problem attains its optimum.

results.title: Weak duality for flux balance analysis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Weak duality for flux balance analysis.

results.title: Strong duality for flux balance analysis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Strong duality for flux balance analysis: a feasible problem has a dual feasible point whose value is the optimal value.

results.title: Concavity of the flux balance optimum in the right-hand side
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The optimal value is concave in the right-hand side `b` on the set of feasible `b`.

results.title: Shadow prices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Shadow prices (Orth, Thiele & Palsson 2010): at a feasible `b`, the metabolite prices `y` of the optimal dual solutions are exactly the supergradients of the optimal value: `fbaValue b' ≤ fbaValue b + y ⬝ᵥ (b' - b)` for every feasible `b'`.

results.title: Uniqueness of Sinkhorn scaling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two diagonal scalings of a positive matrix to doubly stochastic form differ by a positive scalar.

results.title: Symmetric matrix balancing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Symmetric matrix balancing (Sinkhorn 1964; the "equal visibility" normalization of Imakaev et al. 2012): a symmetric matrix with positive entries has a unique positive vector `d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic.

results.title: Total support of a square matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A square matrix has total support if it is nonzero and every positive entry lies on a positive diagonal: for `A i j > 0` there is a permutation `σ` with `σ i = j` and `A k (σ k) > 0` for all `k` (Sinkhorn & Knopp 1967; Csima & Datta 1972).

results.title: Necessity of total support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Necessity of total support (Sinkhorn & Knopp 1967; Csima & Datta 1972): if a positive diagonal scaling `diag(d) A diag(d)` is doubly stochastic, then `A` has total support. The proof uses Birkhoff's theorem. The converse for symmetric nonnegative `A` is `exists_symmetric_balancing_of_hasTotalSupport`.

results.title: Interaction graph of a Boolean network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the interaction graph of `f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1}ⁿ` there is an edge `j → i` when the `i`-th coordinate of `f` depends on the `j`-th variable.

results.title: Acyclic interaction graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The interaction graph of `f` has no directed cycle (loops included).

results.title: Robert's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Robert's theorem (Robert 1980): if the interaction graph of `f : {0,1}ⁿ → {0,1}ⁿ` is acyclic, `f` has a unique fixed point `p`, and every synchronous trajectory reaches it within `n` steps.

results.title: Spanning in-tree rooted at a state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `t : ι → ι` is a spanning in-tree rooted at `r` (each `i ≠ r` points to its parent `t i`): `t r = r` and iterating `t` from any state reaches `r`.

results.title: Total weight of spanning in-trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total weight `∑_t ∏_{i ≠ r} Q i (t i)` of the spanning in-trees rooted at `r`.

results.title: Irreducible rate matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A rate matrix is irreducible if every state reaches every other state through positive jump rates.

results.title: Markov chain tree theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Markov chain tree theorem (King & Altman 1956; Hill 1966): the in-tree weights are invariant for every matrix with zero row sums, `w Q = 0`. The proof matches both sides with the maps `g : ι → ι` whose functional graph has its cycle through `j` (Anantharam & Tsoucas 1989).

results.title: In-tree weights of an irreducible rate matrix are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an irreducible rate matrix every in-tree weight is positive.

results.title: Uniqueness in the Markov chain tree theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an irreducible rate matrix every invariant vector is a multiple of the in-tree weights: the stationary law is proportional, at each state, to the weight of the spanning in-trees rooted there.

results.title: Finitely many dual solutions suffice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite set `T` of pairs `(y, u ⬝ᵥ α - l ⬝ᵥ β)` with `(y, α, β)` dual feasible, such that for every feasible `b` some pair in `T` is optimal: `y ⬝ᵥ b + κ = fbaValue S l u c b`.

results.title: The FBA value is piecewise linear
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are finitely many affine functions `b ↦ y ⬝ᵥ b + κ` whose minimum is the optimal value at every feasible right-hand side `b`.

results.title: Shadow prices are derivatives when unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `b` is an interior point of the set of feasible right-hand sides and `y` is the only metabolite price vector of an optimal dual solution, then the optimal value is differentiable at `b` with derivative `b' ↦ y ⬝ᵥ b'`.
